newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: CAR MAKERS POSITIVE ABOUT TARIFF PLAN
There's been a positive response to the Federal Government's car tariff plan by some of the country's leading car makers.
The Government has opted to freeze tariffs at 15% from the year 2000 for four years, and cut them to 10% in 2005.
The Chief Executive of the Ford Motor Company, David Morgan, believes the car industry will be able to adapt to the gradual fall in tariffs without job losses.
Mr Morgan says it gives the car makers six years to plan and be able to accomodate the eventual drop in tariffs.
Mitsubishi Chief Executive, Mike Quinn, is equally positive, describing it as a very balanced decision.
Mr Quinn says it gives car makers the opportunity to invest with confidence.
MACFARLANE TELLS LONDON AUDIENCE ECONOMIC GROWTH TO PICK UP
Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane, says Australia's economic growth this year would be considerably stronger than it had been in 1996.
Mr Macfarlane made his prediction in London while addressing a Westpac Banking seminar.

Ian Macfarlane told his audience that Australia's latest growth figure of 2.4% cent was a good one, given that the economy was coming out of what he called, a mid-expansion pause. Mr Macfarlane said one of the reasons for his prediction was a run-down in business stocks, which he said were due to be built back up again.
MP CALLS FOR MORE FUNDING TO FIGHT DRUG TRAFFICKING
A Federal MP has described the $13 million dollars the Federal Government plans to spend on its new anti-crime strategy as a "palty sum".
Paul Filing says the Government should provide an extra $100 million each year to combat drug trafficking.
Mr Filing says funding for law enforcement agencies has been cut by more than the cost of the proposed strategy.
He says the funding announced as part of the Government's National Campaign Agianst Violence and Crime will not go to operational policing, but to other programs.
DISCUSSIONS TO SIMPLIFY METAL INDUSTRY AWARDS
Metal trades employers have told unions that workers should be able to cash out award conditions such as penalty loadings.
The employers and union represenatives are negotiating to simplify the metal industry's award, in accordance with the Government's Workplace Relations Act.
The Metal Trades Industries Association told unions it would not adopt a "slash-and-burn" approach to the award, but wants to increase the flexibility of provisions.
The Association says agreement at enterprise level could allow changes in how leave is taken, swapping of penalty loadings for a lump sum, and changes in hours.
Further talks are planned for next month.
CARR AND PM TO DISCUSS EXTORTION, DROUGHT RELIEF
The New South Wales Premier wants tougher uniform laws for those who contaminate food for the purposes of extortion.
Bob Carr will meet with Prime Minister John Howard today, and ask him to endorse the national approach.
Mr Carr says penalties have not been tough enough.
He says there must be a national approach, and says he has Victoria's support.
Mr Carr and the Prime Minister will also discuss drought relief and assistance for the New South Wales sugar industry. The two will meet in Mr Howard's Sydney office this afternoon.
INVESTIGATIONS CONTINUING INTO GIRL'S DEATH
Officers from the Department of Industrial affairs are investigating the death yesterday of a young girl on a shopping trip with her parents in an Adelaide suburb.
The four-year-old was crushed to death when an advertising sign attached to a pillar in a busy mall of the Arndale shopping centre fell on her.
She was rushed to the Womens and Childrens Hospital but was dead on arrival.
Police and investigating officers are compiling a report for the coroner.
ENGLAND ON TARGET FOR FIRST TEST WIN
Victory is within grasp for England after the forst day of the first test of the Ashes tour, following a poor batting display by Australia.
The tourists were bundled out for 118 at Edgebaston; Shane Warne top scored with 47.
In reply, the English finished the day at three for 300, a lead of 82.
Graeme Thorpe on 80 and Nasser Hussain on 83 put on an unbeaten 150 for the fourth wicket.
